{{< include _caveat.qmd >}}

Worked analyses on eco tables, each fetched from the public Redivis endpoint
with the [R package](../r.html) and pinned to a release. Every one runs from a
clean session.

::: {.eco-cards}
<div class="card"><h3><a href="occupancy.html">Single-species site occupancy</a></h3><p>The MacKenzie et al. (2002) model as Kéry and Royle present it in <em>Applied Hierarchical Modeling</em> chapter 10, fit with <code>unmarked</code> to the Swiss willow tit table. A simulator shows why repeat surveys separate ψ from p; then the fit, conditional occupancy of undetected sites, and a goodness-of-fit test that rejects.</p></div>
<div class="card"><h3><a href="cjs.html">Survival from capture histories</a></h3><p>The Cormack-Jolly-Seber model fit with <code>marked</code> to Lebreton et al.'s European dipper, reproducing the 1983 flood effect, then to 28 capture-history tables from elephant seals to cacti. A simulator shows why recapture separates survival from detection; U-CARE tests show where the model fails.</p></div>
<div class="card"><h3><a href="species_items.html">Species as items: community occupancy</a></h3><p>A community survey is a site-by-species table, and the multispecies occupancy model gives every site a latent quantity and every species its own parameters, drawn from a community. Fit to 34 boreal birds at 564 recorders with and without detection, then with spOccupancy: ignoring detection understates every species by an amount set by how detectable it is, a site variable found from the species alone recovers the harvest-edge gradient, and a sparse camera table shows what pooling species can and cannot do.</p></div>
:::
